newsitem.title: USA: Utilities press U.S. Congress to cut TVA subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Utilities press U.S. Congress to cut TVA subsidies.

text.p: Investor-owned utilities in areas surrounding the Tennessee Valley Authority's customer territory are stepping up their bid to convince Congress to cut off subsidies to the federally backed power generator.

The newly-formed TVA Reform Alliance, led by utilities owned by Southern Company, Tuesday held a news conference to publicize moves by lawmakers to get rid of TVA tax breaks and funding for its land and water programs.
They also pointed to a consultant's report released last month which said TVA receives $1.2 billion annually in subsidies, including tax breaks and access to cheap power.

The campaign against TVA, which has 7.3 million customers, is part of the larger lobbying effort by big utilities to ensure that if Congress makes states break utility monopolies, it should put all power generators on an equal footing.
"It's not fair that consumers around the nation should be subsidizing electricity in this seven-state area," said Rep. Rodney Frelinghuysen, R-N.J.
Frelinghuysen, who is on the House panel that provides money for TVA, has introduced legislation to cut off the annual $106 million in federal funding for TVA's non-power programs this October.
"To balance the federal budget by 2002...this is the type of subsidy that should come to a screeching halt," he said at the news conference.
He said the land and water programs TVA runs for the federal government should be paid for through a electricity rate increase, which TVA customers have not had in 10 years.
In retaliation to the report, TVA last month asked House lawmakers to investigate tax breaks enjoyed by investor-owned utilities.

An aide to Rep. Bob Franks, R-N.J., who introduced a bill to cut off funding for TVA's non-power programs in October 1999, as requested by TVA, said one of the main goals of his bill was to ensure that TVA could not use offers of cheap power to lure businesses away from his state.
